scope: Finite-sample unbiasedness of the usual bootstrap/Feynman-Kac particle normalising-constant estimator when each generation's finite offspring count N_t and generation-t tuning are measurable with respect to the completed past F_{t-1}, resampling satisfies the conditional proper-weighting identity, and the generation-t kernel/potential are fixed before current-generation randomness. No claim is made for same-generation adaptive target/proposal changes, random post-resampling population rules outside this conditioning argument, variance dominance, or real-agent performance.

independent_primary_checks.source: Dau and Chopin, Waste-Free Sequential Monte Carlo, JRSS B 84(1), 2022
independent_primary_checks.observed_support: Proposition 2 explicitly states unbiasedness of the product-of-average-potential normalising-constant estimator and reduces it to standard SMC unbiasedness. This supports the base Feynman-Kac induction, but the paper excerpt independently checked here does not state the exact predictable-random-N_t extension.

independent_primary_checks.source: Douc, Cappe, Moulines, Comparison of Resampling Schemes for Particle Filtering, arXiv:cs/0507025
independent_primary_checks.observed_support: The paper defines the proper-weighting condition E[N^i | G]=n w_i, explicitly allows offspring count n different from parent count m, and states stratified resampling satisfies the target weighted empirical expectation identity. This directly supports the conditional resampling step used by the worker lemma.

independent_primary_checks.source: Zhou, Johansen, Aston, Toward Automatic Model Comparison: An Adaptive Sequential Monte Carlo Approach
independent_primary_checks.observed_support: The paper warns that the standard normalising-constant estimate need not be unbiased under generic adaptive techniques. This supports the worker's restrictive scope boundary and prevents promotion to unrestricted adaptive-SMC unbiasedness.

worker_proof_sketch_core_steps: Condition on F_{t-1}, making predictable N_t and tuning fixed for the current step.
Apply conditional proper-weighting of resampling even when offspring n differs from parent m.
Apply the fixed generation-t Feynman-Kac operator under propagation/potential expectation.
Use tower expectation to continue the standard unnormalised-measure induction; set f=1 for Z_t.

grading.uncertainty: The checked primary sources establish the two essential components: standard SMC normalising-constant unbiasedness and proper-weighting/stratified resampling for n distinct from m. Conditionalising on the completed past makes a predictable finite N_t fixed within the current step, so the worker's tower-expectation extension is mathematically well motivated. However, this bounded slice did not independently locate a published theorem stated in exactly the worker's predictable-random-N_t form or machine-check the full induction. Generic adaptive SMC can lose unbiasedness, so the grade applies only to the explicit predictability/fixed-current-increment scope.
